en: The *Kalyāṇatriṃśatikā-stotra*: Having thus resolved through body, speech, mind, and intellect, I constantly perform praise, worship, and circumambulation of her. (1)
Salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again—to that Goddess who effects the creation and destruction of all sentient beings. (2)
To that Goddess who is established as the protector of all beings—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 3 ||
Salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation again and again—to that Goddess who stands in the form of a deity among the goddesses of the gods. || 4 ||
Salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again—to that Goddess who is terrifying in form, burning the Daityas who are difficult to subdue. || 5 ||
To that Goddess who is the thousand-faced Nāginī of all the nāgas—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 6 ||
Salutations to that Goddess who dwells in the seven netherworlds in a peaceful form; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.
Salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, repeated salutations to that Goddess who is the Mother of the Vedas, the Consciousness-Mother (Cidambikā) of men and women. || 8 ||
To that Goddess who is worshipped by the Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra castes—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! (9)
Salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation again and again—to that goddess of great supernatural power who protects the worlds of the departed spirits. || 10 ||
Salutation to that Goddess who delivers all those among the animals and destroys their torment; salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation again and again.
Salutations to that Goddess, the mother of those in hell and of all who partake in suffering; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again. (12)
Salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, repeated salutations to her—the Goddess who is the destroyer of the sixteen hells. || 13 ||

Salutation to that Goddess who has been made difficult to overcome by those possessed of hatred and passion, and by the deluded; salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation, salutation! (14)
To that Goddess who, through desire and anger, abides in the form of wrath—to her be homage, to her be homage, to her be homage, homage again and again! (15)
Salutations to that Goddess who has delayed for the sake of transcending greed and gain; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again! (16)
To that Goddess who is the mother of Māyā, the Vajrayoginī of all mothers—to her, salutation; to her, salutation; to her, salutation; salutation, salutation! (17)
Salutations to that Goddess, who destroys kings, thieves, fire, lions, and enemies; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again. || 18 ||
Salutation to that Goddess, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation again and again—she who delivers one from the fear of water, serpents, nāgas, and famine. || 19 ||
To that Goddess who is established in the five elements, in the moon, and in the sun—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 20 ||
Salutation to that Goddess who is the temporal limit of the elements, who moves within the vowels and consonants; salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation again and again.

Salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again—to that Goddess who is the sovereign of all sacred seats (pīṭhas) and the secondary manifestation (upachandikā) in the form of the field (kṣetra). || 22 ||
To that goddess who is called Pīlava and joined with Upapīlava—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage! || 23 ||

Salutations to that Goddess who, adorned by the zodiac signs and the ascendant, resides in the twelfth wheel; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again. || 24 ||
Salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, repeated salutations; to that Goddess whose moon-like face is fully blossomed in the region of the six limbs. || 25 ||
Salutation to that Goddess, the Supreme Sovereign who moves within the fierce wheels; salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation again and again. || 26 ||
To that Goddess who moves through body, speech, and mind in the form of mantra—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 27 ||
Salutations to that Goddess who is pure of soul, the bestower of fortune, prosperity, accomplishment, and strength;
salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again. || 28 ||
Salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again—to that goddess who always brings auspiciousness to all living beings. (29)
The wise person who recites this, endowed with devotion to the Goddess, swiftly attains Buddhahood—auspicious, auspicious, and blissful. (30)
The *Kalyāṇatriṃśatikāstotra*, a hymn of thirty auspicious verses to the Vajradevī who dwells in the three glorious bodies, is complete.
